notes: Blue Tehran municipal street plate with red number box (۴۲) and District 1 label; Persian digits. The green arrow sign below ('حسینیه بزرگ / دزاشیب', Great Hosseiniyeh of Dezashib) is a distractor/secondary sign. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.

author: Bernard Gagnon
attribution: Photo: Bernard Gagnon, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Street_sign_in_Yazd.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Two plates on a mud-brick wall in Yazd: upper blue/white postcode plate (header 'پلاک کد پستی', small side texts 'شهرداری یزد' and 'اداره کل پست استان یزد' not labelled), lower metal municipal house-number plate 'شهرداری یزد' / ۲۶. Digits are Persian (U+06F0-06F9); the 4 in the postcode is drawn in the open ٤-like style common on Iranian signage and is encoded as Persian ۴. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.

notes: Yellow rooftop letters naming the Jafari shopping centre, Khorsand Boulevard, Kazerun; a power line crosses the letters. Car plates incidental. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.

author: blondinrikard

notes: Engraved wooden cafe sign in Tehran under deep red light, strongly angled and slightly soft. The 'o' in Romance is a heart-like shape. The engraved Persian word above (probably 'رومنس') and a small mark between the two words are too shallow to read with certainty and are not transcribed.

author: blondinrikard

notes: Red neon-tube letters on a frame against trees and sky, Isfahan (Restaurant Maral). Unlit daytime shot but letter shapes are clear.

author: blondinrikard
attribution: Photo: blondinrikard, CC BY 2.0, via Flickr. Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/44093058@N06/14354457311. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Long bilingual name banner on brick wall, Isfahan. The Persian line is cut off at the right frame edge: the first letter ب of باغ is outside the photo, so only 'اغ موزه چهلستون' is visible. Tiny text in the middle of the banner is unreadable and not labelled.

author: Behnam9395
attribution: Photo: Behnam9395, CC0 1.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Khorsand_Boulevard_of_Kazerun_12.jpg. License: http://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/deed.en. Unmodified original.
notes: Cluster of six bilingual arrow-shaped direction blades on a pole at a roundabout on Khorsand Boulevard, Kazerun; small in the frame (lower right). Left column (arrows left) listed first, then right column (arrows right). 'Parishan Lake' blade is blue, others white. A partly hidden seventh blade sits below on the right.

author: Alen Ištoković
attribution: Photo: Alen Ištoković, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:UNESCO_sign,_Takht-e_Soleyman_-_panoramio.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Black granite UNESCO World Heritage plaque, photographed at a steep angle. Only the site-name lines are labelled: Persian nastaliq title on the right half, English title on the left half. The small body text (UNESCO convention wording, Persian paragraph) is too small/angled to transcribe. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.

Tiz kardan-e anva'-e chaghu, gheychi va mashinha-ye (sharpening all kinds of knives, scissors and ...)

notes: Hanging shop sign under a bazaar vault in Yazd, seen from below at an angle; name in red, services in blue-black, a hair clipper (MOSER) picture and red arrow at left. Phone number in Persian digits ۶۲۲۲۷۵۹ sits on the same physical row as 'تلفن' and 'ریش تراش'. A wire crosses the lower text. Words are run together as painted (تعمیرلوازم, ودیگهای, وماشینهای).
